paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees "do not practice what they preach" (Matthew 23:3). Good words are not the problem. The problem is a gap between what a person says and how that person lives. So Jesus wants you to hold both together, with the same words on your lips and in your life.

Look at what He says drives that gap. "All their deeds are done for men to see" (Matthew 23:5). They love the places of honor, the chief seats and the title of 'Rabbi' (Matthew 23:6-7). Friend, I get it. Everybody likes a spotlight, and I've stood on this gold base long enough to know how nice a little applause feels. But Jesus points you away from it, because you have one Teacher, one Father in heaven and one Instructor, the Christ (Matthew 23:8-10).

So what's the better way? "The greatest among you shall be your servant" (Matthew 23:11). "For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted" (Matthew 23:12). Don't chase the seat, friend. Go lift something for somebody, especially the loads you could easily walk past. And keep your apron ON, because Jesus isn't done teaching yet.
